title: USACE continues its Hurricane Ian support to FEMA, Florida
description: Doug Weber, USACE infrastruture assessment team subject matter expert and Seattle District employee, discusses what the team is doing to support FEMA and the state of Florida in their Hurricane Ian recovery efforts.
keywords: FEMA, jacksonville district, Ian, Hurricane Ian, HurricaneIan22, USACE
unit_name: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Jacksonville District

transcript.text: I'm Doug Webber . I'm infrastructure
assessment subject matter expert . I've
been deployed down here to help assess
buildings for habitability , basically
recommend safety ratings . I'm out here
at Fort Myers Beach and we have wrapped
up the rapid assessments . We've had
teams out looking at about 3200
buildings Really every building out on
the beach to do a rapid assessment to
determine if they were safe to enter
and to live in . And now we're
following up with detailed assessment .
So some of the buildings are larger and
more complicated and we have 220
buildings that were doing follow up
detailed assessments . The purpose of
the details when they did the rap
assessments , it's intended to be less
than half an hour external only . And
um a lot of the buildings that's all
that's necessary to determine the
safety but some you can't see what's up
on the roof . You need to go inside and
look at the structure , the connections
and so the purpose of the detailed is
to come back and really dig in and get
a more thorough look and still to
determine a safety rating and make sure
the building is safe to enter and so
what it means to them is if there's a
green tag then the building is safe to
enter and occupy , there could still be
damage . Certainly is , you know ,
damages , but it is a safe building
from a structural standpoint to be in
and inhabit . If it has a yellow tag
then it's restricted use . You you can
go in but there might be areas that are
restricted and unsafe or there's enough
dangers that you really shouldn't stay
there . But you can go in and out to
get your belongings or to begin working
on your facility for a red tag building ,
it's unsafe to enter .
There's just to higher risk
to someone going in and out of that
building until um safety measures have
been taken , could be shoring or other
measures you know , to make the
building more safe to enter . So we're
working with the city , the county and
the state , we have both Corps of
Engineers assessors and assessors that
have come from other areas in florida .
So we're working together of our
assessments are recommendations that go
back to the state , the county and to
the city and ultimately , the city
building officials in the county are
responsible for determining the placard
and the safety rating for the buildings .
Mhm .
